text: The dragon Fortissax formed a genuine bond of friendship with Godwyn the Golden, Godfrey and Marika's noble, widely beloved firstborn son.
Marika was originally a Newman (Numen), a rare people from outside the Lands Between, chosen and brought to the Lands Between by the Greater Will to serve as their vassal.
Marika was chosen as an Empyrean candidate by the Two Fingers and became a god at the Gate of Divinity in Anor Ilim.
Marika's first consort in the ritual of godhood was Hoarah Loux, a warrior chieftain from the Badlands, who would become known as Godfrey, the first Elden Lord.
Godfrey was a chieftain from the Badlands, an extraordinarily powerful warrior consumed by a lust for battle.
Marika chose Hoarah Loux as her consort because he was the best warrior in the world, needed to conquer resisting peoples for the Golden Order.
Radagon previously married Renala, Queen of the Full Moon, after defeating her sorcerers in battle and proposing peace through union.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: Radagon and Renala had three children together: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: Because Marika and Radagon are the same being, Renala was in effect abandoned by the very god she had helped ascend, though she does not consciously realize this.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: At Raya Lucaria Academy's Grand Library, Renala clutches an amber egg given to her by Radagon as a parting gift, believing it contains her beloved Radagon and refusing to accept his departure.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: Because Marika and Radagon are a single god, their children Miquella and Malenia were described in-game as born of a single god and were cursed from birth.
Miquella was cursed with eternal youth, forever trapped in a child's body, unable to grow into the mature form required for godhood.
Malenia was born harboring the Scarlet Rot, marked by the God of Scarlet Rot from birth per the Remembrance of the Rot Goddess, a corruption that eventually consumed her eye, arm, and leg.
Godfrey and Marika's twin omen sons, Morgott and Mohg, were hidden and thrown into the sewers beneath Leyndell at birth because their crucible-like deformities were considered shameful.
Morgott, though shunned and reviled in Leyndell his entire life, eventually escaped confinement and dedicated his life to protecting the city that had reviled him.
Mohg escaped his confinement but turned toward worship of an outer god called the Formless Mother, building a hidden palace of blood devotion around a wound in the earth.
After being exiled, Godfrey reverted to being Hoarah Loux, wandering and fighting for the pure pleasure of combat while waiting for Marika's promise to be fulfilled.
Godfrey served the Golden Order with absolute commitment and was exiled for having run out of wars to fight.

Radahn is a massive lion-armored general who studied gravitational magic in Sellia, a Caelid town known for sorcerers who studied stars and cosmic forces, partly so he could continue riding his small horse Leonard, whom he'd owned since childhood, without crushing it under his growing size.
Radahn used gravity magic to halt the movement of the stars, locking the constellations in place to prevent an unwanted destiny.

Rykard became the Lord of Blasphemy, a ruthless justiciar and son of Rennala and Radagon who presides over Mt. Gelmir, merging with a great serpent god and turning Volcano Manor into a haven for rebels and assassins who reject the Greater Will's authority.
Rykard was served by the Gelmir Knights, and the lava sorceries usable by the Tarnished were created by him, some derived from old Mt. Gelmir hexes.
The Taker's Cameo item description implies Rykard believed Marika and her Order ruled by force, prompting him to swear himself to blasphemy and seek to overthrow them.

Ranni the Witch renounced her flesh and transferred her soul into a porcelain doll modeled after a mentor she loved, dying in the flesh on the Night of the Black Knives in order to preserve the freedom of her soul and set her plan in motion.
Ranni was an Empyrean, a candidate to become the next god of the Lands Between under the Greater Will; although not born a demigod, she became eligible due to Radagon's unity with Marika.
Ranni wanted to escape the fate chosen for her by the Two Fingers and refused to continue Marika's cycle of divine control.
Miquella envisioned a world without discrimination that would welcome those rejected by the Golden Order, including albinaurics, the misbegotten, and omens.
Miquella developed a theology of 'unalloyed gold,' a form of divine power independent of the Greater Will, and used it to grow the Haligtree as a sanctuary.
Miquella possesses a supernatural charm that compels affection from others, including demigods, which he has used deliberately to further his goals.
Malenia serves as Miquella's sworn protector and champion, and is said to have never lost a battle except her final one.
Godrick the Grafted was a weak descendant of Godfrey's line who surgically attached the limbs of conquered warriors to his own body to compensate for his inadequacy.
Vyke, a tarnished, was according to item descriptions closer to becoming Elden Lord than anyone before the player character.
Ranni is introduced to the player in a tower in northern Liurnia, one of three towers belonging to her and her brothers, once her family's home before her father Radagon left to return to Marika.
Ranni appears as a young woman with pale blue skin and silver hair inhabiting a small doll body.
Ranni's retinue includes Blaidd, a half-man half-wolf sworn to serve her; Iji, an ancient blacksmith; and Sellen, a snow witch whose loyalty is complex.
Alexander the Iron Fist is a giant jar, a living vessel called a 'jarhead' containing the remains of great warriors absorbed into it.
Alexander is found stuck in the ground up to his shoulders, calling cheerfully for help, and wants to grow stronger by absorbing the remains of great warriors.
Alexander travels toward the Radahn Festival out of genuine joy at the prospect of fighting alongside great warriors.
At the end of his questline, Alexander requests to be defeated by the player so his absorbed essence can be carried forward.
Nepheli Loux is the granddaughter of Gideon Ofnir, the all-knowing leader of the Round Table Hold faction.
Nepheli Loux is the adoptive daughter of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, who named her his heir even in exile.
Nepheli Loux is the adoptive daughter of Sir Gideon Ofnir, who took her in when she became Tarnished after losing grace.
Nepheli's questline involves confronting the horror of Stormveil's population being experimented on and turned into shambling creatures by Godrick.
Nepheli Loux loses faith in Sir Gideon Ofnir after learning he orchestrated the attack on the Village of the Albinaurics.
It is speculated that Nepheli Loux has ties to Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, based on sharing the surname Loux with Hoarah Loux and Kenneth Haight deeming her worthy to lead Limgrave.
Fia, the Deathbed Companion, resides in the Round Table Hold and offers an embrace that grants a buff and a debuff simultaneously.
Fia collects deathbeds, the moments of heroes' final rest, carrying them inside her body to eventually create the Prince of Death made possible by Godwyn's incomplete demise.
The Tarnished is a being who once possessed the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, died, and endured a strange persistence that being Tarnished grants.

Melina walks beside the Tarnished as a guide, tending the Sites of Grace, and has no grace or permanent vessel of her own, appearing only through temporary forms; she serves as the Tarnished's Finger Maiden in exchange for being taken to the Erdtree and later the Mountaintops of the Giants.
Melina offers the Tarnished fragments of information and a kindness that seems genuine despite being largely unexplained.

Melina's true goal, only understood at the end of the story, is to sacrifice herself as kindling to burn open the Erdtree so the Tarnished can enter it; at the Forge of the Giants she carries this out, stating she does not know what she will become but does not regret the choice.
Melina describes herself as someone born at the foot of the Erdtree who was given a purpose by her mother, whom she believes can be found there, leading to speculation that her mother is Marika.
Melina may be a child of Marika existing outside conventional demigod lineages, or a soul given form by the Erdtree, or a deliberate contingency created by Marika.
Melina appears at Sites of Grace as though existing at the margins of the world rather than at its center.
Melina can recall echoes of Queen Marika's past actions and words when spoken to at Sites of Grace.
Melina holds contempt for the Frenzied Flame and believes its lord is no true Lord.
If the Tarnished takes the Frenzied Flame before the event at the Forge of the Giants, Melina will leave and threaten to deliver Destined Death.
Goldmask, using the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, concluded that the flaws of the Golden Order come from the fact that gods are as flawed and fickle as the mortals they govern.
Fia is empathetic toward and devoted to the cause of Those Who Live in Death, considering herself their guardian.
Godwyn's incomplete death produced an entity called the Death Prince, combining Godwyn's lingering flesh presence with the rune of death.

The Dung Eater has committed atrocities against both the dead and the living and wants to spread his personal curse to all beings in the Lands Between and all future generations, so everyone is equally defiled, by gestating the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse.
entities: Mending Rune of the Fell Curse

text: Miquella's compassion was genuine, but his methods were controlling and manipulative in ways his good intentions do not fully excuse.
Malenia gave everything for her brother's cause and is depicted as still waiting for him to return.
Fia held dying Tarnished in her arms out of compassion because she believed someone needed to.
Goldmask sat in silence at the edge of a great ruin, working out the nature of the universe without writing anything down, believing the right person would understand without words.
General Radahn is described as 'the conqueror of the stars' and Malenia the Severed as 'the Blade of Miquella'.
The White Masks at Mohgwyn Palace were abducted by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and turned into Bloody Fingers through a ritual involving his Omen blood.
Of the four White Masks encountered, only Varre was able to withstand and tame the accursed blood.
White Mask Varre remains loyal to the Mohgwyn Dynasty and tries to indoctrinate the Tarnished into it.
At the end of his questline, White Mask Varre, forsaken by Mohg, still calls out to him and blesses the Mohgwyn Dynasty as he dies.
Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is a samurai from the Land of Reeds who hunts down Bloody Fingers.
Yura's biggest target is Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a Tarnished he holds in high regard.
Yura warns that those who partake in Dragon Communion eventually lose their humanity.
Some Bloody Fingers encountered by the Tarnished have been swayed by Mohg, the Lord of Blood.
Sorcerer Rogier was once a scholar seeking the truth behind the Night of the Black Knives.
Rogier's scholarly pursuits led him under Stormveil Castle, where he disturbed a corpse and became afflicted with Death.
Unlike D, who sees Those Who Live in Death as a threat to the Golden Order, Rogier is empathetic toward them.
Finishing Rogier's quest reveals insights about the Night of the Black Knives before he succumbs to his affliction.
Fia is a Tarnished Deathbed Companion driven from her home when awoken by the guidance of grace.
A Deathbed Companion receives warmth and life from champions and then lies with the remains of an exalted noble to revive them, a practice revered in Fia's homeland.
Fia's champions include Rogier and Lionel the Lionhearted, a knight who claims to be her father.

By combining Ranni's half of the Cursemark of Death from the Divine Tower of Liurnia with Godwyn's half from D, Fia implies Godwyn could be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince through her role as his Deathbed Companion.
D, Hunter of the Dead is a devout follower of the Golden Order who hunts Those Who Live in Death, especially Tibia Mariners for their Deathroot.
D has a twin brother whose name is implied to be Darian.
D and his twin brother share the same soul and body, and cannot be conscious at the same time despite having separate bodies and minds.
D and his twin found comfort in the Golden Order, which was the one order that did not consider them cursed.
D states that Those Who Live in Death violate the principles of the Golden Order and must be exterminated.
D's twin brother is inferred to be named Devin based on D's voicelines.
D, Beholder of Death can be found slumbering in Siofra Aqueduct while D is alive, and grieving there if D is dead.
D's twin brother swears revenge on his brother's killer, whether it be Fia or the Tarnished, when given his brother's armor.
Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is a large beastman who hungers for Deathroot.
D was previously in charge of hunting and providing Deathroot to Gurranq before the Tarnished took over.
It is heavily implied that the Beast Clergyman found in Crumbling Farum Azula is Gurranq himself, and that Gurranq is Maliketh, the Black Blade.
Maliketh is Marika's Shadow, bestowed on her by the Greater Will as an Empyrean, similar to how Blaidd is Ranni's Shadow.
According to the Stone of Gurranq, Maliketh was a ferocious warrior whose name meant 'Death of the Demigods'.
Maliketh's Remembrance implies he was betrayed by Marika, though the details are unknown.
Roderika is a Tarnished driven away from her home across the sea, and her cloak implies she was once royalty.
Roderika met White Mask Varre, who gave her the same advice he gives the Tarnished: to seek Godrick and his Great Rune at Stormveil Castle.
The men escorting Roderika at Stormhill were taken and sacrificed for grafting, leaving her guilt-ridden for being too afraid to join them.
Roderika moves to the Roundtable Hold and is trained by Smithing Master Hewg to become a skillful spirit tuner.
Roderika stays behind with Hewg even as the Roundtable Hold burns, to repay his kindness.
Smithing Master Hewg is a misbegotten chained and imprisoned at the Roundtable Hold, tasked by Queen Marika with forging a weapon strong enough to kill a god.
Hewg believes the Tarnished will become Elden Lord, and states so before losing his memory completely.
Kenneth Haight is a member of Erdtree royalty and self-proclaimed rightful leader of Limgrave, owner of Fort Haight.
Kenneth Haight looks down on Godrick for his cowardly actions during the Shattering and for lacking proper lineage to rule.
After retaking Fort Haight, Kenneth Haight seeks an eligible candidate to rule Limgrave and eventually finds Nepheli Loux.
Gatekeeper Gostoc is the gatekeeper of Stormveil Castle who nonetheless informs the Tarnished of a safer side passage.
Gostoc secretly follows and steals a portion of the Tarnished's Golden Runes each time they are defeated in the castle.
Gostoc holds contempt for Godrick, having been mistreated by him, and longs for freedom from his duties.
When Nepheli Loux takes the throne, Gostoc is happy to return to his duties.
Boc the Seamster is a demi-human outcast who admires his late mother, a skilled seamstress.
Boc was expelled from the Coastal Cave and had his possessions stolen by other demi-humans.
After the Tarnished helps Boc reclaim his Sewing Needle and Tailoring Tools, he offers to tailor their armor.
The Tarnished can help Boc by giving him a Larval Tear to change his appearance or by telling him he is beautiful, and he is grateful either way.
Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order whose armor implies he once foretold an inauspicious prophecy.
Corhyn leaves the Roundtable Hold in search of Goldmask, a scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism.
Corhyn acts as Goldmask's scribe, translating his finger movements into written records.
Corhyn begins to question Goldmask's intentions after learning of his reservations toward the Golden Order.
Goldmask is a famed scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism who does not speak, communicating instead through rhythmic hand and finger movements.
Goldmask once lamented that hunters of Those Who Live in Death had become fanatics who hunted merely to have an evil to fight.
Gowry is a Kindred of Rot disguised as an old sage and was Millicent's caretaker as a child.
Gowry found Millicent and presumably her sisters as babies in the swamp of Aeonia and raised them hoping they would become scarlet valkyries under Malenia.
Gowry saw the most potential in Millicent among the sisters to follow Malenia's path.
At the end of Millicent's quest, Gowry asks the Tarnished to help Millicent's sisters attack her, believing betrayal will trigger her to 'bloom'.
Millicent is a daughter of Malenia, sharing her mother's red hair, missing arm from scarlet rot, and swordsmanship style.
Due to scarlet rot, Millicent does not remember her childhood with Gowry despite feeling familiarity at his shack.
After being cured with the Unalloyed Golden Needle, Millicent seeks out Malenia to help her resist the scarlet rot.
Millicent is ambushed by her sisters at Elphael before reaching Malenia.
If defended by the Tarnished, Millicent reveals she knows what Gowry hoped she would become, then removes the golden needle and succumbs to scarlet rot to remain herself.
Irina is the blind daughter of Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne.
Irina escaped Castle Morne with her father's and attendants' help after the Misbegotten serving the castle rebelled.
Irina asks the Tarnished to deliver a letter persuading her father to leave the castle, but she is murdered before their reunion.
The large sword found by Irina's corpse implies an escaped Misbegotten from Castle Morne was her killer.
Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, was ordained by Godrick and stays to protect the castle's Grafted Blade Greatsword even as attendants flee the Misbegotten rebellion.
After finding Irina's body, Edgar regrets failing to protect her and swears vengeance on her killers.
Edgar can later be found as an invader at Revengers Shack, and the Shabriri Grape he drops suggests he succumbed to madness from Irina's death.
Hyetta is a blind young woman who resembles Irina and can perceive light by consuming Shabriri Grapes.
Hyetta is initially disgusted that Shabriri Grapes are human eyes but accepts it as necessary to become a finger maiden.
Hyetta mentions other beings with trembling hands and emaciated fingers have also given her Shabriri Grapes.
Completing Hyetta's quest and helping her become a Finger Maiden reveals more information on the Three Fingers and the Frenzied Flame.
Shabriri is a mysterious figure calling himself chaos incarnate, inhabiting the body of Yura, who he claims willingly gave it up.
When met at the Mountaintops of the Giants, Shabriri tries to persuade the Tarnished to become Lord of Frenzied Flame and shares information on the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Ranni the Witch is the daughter of Rennala and Radagon.
Ranni discovered her own full moon, Ranni's Dark Moon, and learned cold sorceries from the mysterious Snow Witch she encountered in the woods.
Ranni has held Blaidd and Iji dear since childhood.
Ranni defeated the Glintstone Dragon Adula, who then swore allegiance to her.
Blaidd is the half-wolven Shadow of Ranni, granted to her by the Two Fingers when she became an Empyrean.
Blaidd's loyalty lies only with Ranni, whom he considers family, despite being an agent of the Two Fingers.
Even in madness, Blaidd continued to defy his fate and remain faithful to Ranni.
War Counselor Iji is the only friendly Troll the Tarnished encounters, serving as the Carian royal family's blacksmith.
Iji also serves as Ranni's war counselor, providing guidance on the lost city of Nokron.
Iji has watched over Blaidd and Ranni since they were children.
Iji's Mirrorhelm implies he feared the consequences of his treachery against the Greater Will.
Preceptor Seluvis is a magic preceptor serving the Carian Royal family and currently aids Ranni in her search for the dark path.
Seluvis helped Sellen in some way when she was initially exiled from the academy, though Sellen does not seem fond of him.
Seluvis reveals a scheme to betray Ranni and add her, a demigod, to his puppet collection.
It is speculated that Seluvis and Pidia have a connection due to their shared affinity for puppets.
Merchant Kale is one of the nomadic merchants the Tarnished can buy from, acquainted with Blaidd who calls him a busybody.
Kale describes the nomadic clan as spiteful, suggesting their summoning of the frenzied flame was an act of spite.
Witch-Hunter Jerren was originally a nomadic wanderer who became a guest of the Carian royal family, befriending Ranni, Iji, and Radahn.
Jerren promised Ranni and Iji he would slay the Graven Witch Sellen, a longstanding enemy of the Carian family who had committed atrocities against fellow sorcerers.
Jerren wields the Flamberge, a symbol of Redmane Castle, and heralds the beginning of the war festival when first met.
Sorceress Sellen was one of the most promising sorcerers in the history of Raya Lucaria Academy and had a unique glintstone crown.
Sellen was exiled from Raya Lucaria Academy for her obsession with the forbidden primeval current.
Master Lusat and Master Azur were other primeval sorcerers banished from the Academy, and both had their minds broken by glimpsing the primeval current.
According to Jerren, Sellen has killed many fellow sorcerers in her studies.
Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins by the Academy and the Carian Royal Family due to her forbidden pursuits.
The Tarnished can help Sellen transplant her primeval glintstone, essentially her soul, into another compatible body to free her.
Thops is a glintstone sorcerer from Raya Lucaria Academy nicknamed 'Thops the Bluntstone' for lacking talent for powerful sorceries.
If aided, Thops completes his lifelong project, creating Thops's Barrier, a defensive glintstone sorcery that deflects sorceries and incantations back at the caster.
Miriel, Pastor of Vows is a large turtle and steward of the Church of Vows who teaches Absolution though he does not require it himself.
Miriel is well-versed in the history of Rennala and Radagon's union and teaches the Tarnished sorceries and incantations.
Unlike Corhyn, who deems non-Golden Order incantations heresy, Miriel is open-minded toward all sorcery and incantation scrolls given to him.
Albus is a first-generation Albinauric; first-generation Albinaurics were created with defective legs that prevented walking, and when their legs fade, their life fades too.
The Tarnished finds Albus disguised as a pot to escape Gideon's subordinates attacking the Village of the Albinaurics.
Latenna is a first-generation Albinauric and one of many wolf-riding Albinauric archers.
Latenna was interrogated by an agent of Sir Gideon Ofnir, or possibly Gideon himself, about the second half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, leading to the death of her wolf Lobo.
If approached with the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Latenna asks the Tarnished to take her to Apostate Derelict in exchange for revealing the location of the left half.
At Apostate Derelict, Latenna transfers a birthing droplet to a large Albinauric named Phillia, said to be connected to creating new life for the Albinaurics.
Ensha of the Royal Remains is Sir Gideon Ofnir's silent right-hand man.
Ensha's armor, the Royal Remains Set, and his weapon, the Clinging Bone, suggest he is the reanimated remains of a king known as the Soulless King.

It is speculated from Gideon's dialogue that Ensha was tasked with finding both halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion and attacks the Tarnished at the Roundtable Hold to take whichever half they have found.
Tanith is consort to Lord Rykard and the adoptive mother of Rya.
Tanith worked as a dancer in a foreign land until she caught Lord Rykard's eye and became his consort.

Tanith stayed by Rykard's side even after he swore himself to blasphemy and merged with the God-Devouring Serpent, even when his men turned against him and even when she was offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness as an escape.
Bernahl is an Ash of War teacher the Tarnished can first meet in Stormhill.
Bernahl was said to be a Tarnished worthy of becoming Elden Lord, following his destined path without doubt, until his maiden threw herself into 'the fire'.
The Tarnished can later find Bernahl as a recusant at Volcano Manor.
After Rykard is defeated, Bernahl denounces the Greater Will and vows to fell them on behalf of his brother.
Rya's real name is Zorayas, and she is a Man-Serpent disguised as a human working as the scout for Volcano Manor.
Only the Tarnished and Rya's adoptive mother Tanith know of Rya's true serpent form.
Tanith told Rya that she was born by the grace of a great king, but Rya later becomes suspicious of Volcano Manor's secrets and confronts Tanith.
A talisman left behind at the end of Rya's questline suggests her true mother was Daedicar, a woman said to have birthed multiple grotesque children through countless acts of adultery.
Patches the Untethered is a bandit who tricks unsuspecting people into death traps and entrapment schemes.
If spared, Patches sells the Tarnished various goods presumably looted from the corpses of those he successfully tricked.
Patches mentions his band of bandits is made up of foot soldiers and survivors of defeated armies left to fend for themselves.
Patches has taken a liking to Tanith and risks himself to obtain the Dancer's Castanets, hoping to restore her mind after Rykard's defeat.
Diallos is the youngest son of House Hoslow and lives in the shadow of his elder brother, Juno Hoslow.
Unlike Juno, a formidable fighter, Diallos is timid, which does not fit his family's bloodshed-focused motto.
Despite their differences, Diallos and Juno care deeply for each other, with Juno doting on Diallos and Diallos looking up to him.
Diallos hopes to become a champion like his brother but grows disillusioned and seeks a different purpose.
Jar-Bairn is a young jar living in Jarburg, a secret village of peaceful Living Jars.
Jar-Bairn is one of the few Living Jars capable of speaking to the Tarnished and is a warrior jar like his uncle Alexander.
Jar-Bairn can be found talking in his sleep about reuniting with Alexander, poachers destroying the Living Pots at Jarburg, or Diallos taking care of him.
Iron Fist Alexander is an older Living Jar who left Jarburg to seek great battle and hone his skills.
Warrior jars like Alexander are Living Jars filled with the remains of warriors, destined to leave home and journey alone to become great champions.
Blackguard Big Boggart is a Tarnished and former criminal selling boiled prawns and crabs, first at the Boilprawn Shack and later outside the royal capital.
Boggart may have previously been convicted of thievery, having stolen Rya's necklace.
Boggart used to be cellmates with Dung Eater, witnessing him defile a friend's body with the Seedbed Curse, the most harrowing experience of Boggart's life.
Dung Eater is a Tarnished who bears the heart of an Omen, as suggested by his armor.
Even before returning to the Lands Between, Dung Eater was a merciless killer who defiled his victims' corpses with Seedbed Curses, cursing their souls to never return to the Erdtree.
Enia is a Finger Reader Crone the Tarnished encounters at the Roundtable Hold, interpreting the wisdom of the Greater Will through the Two Fingers.
Unlike other finger readers who become frantic after losing their Two Fingers, Enia remains calm.
Despite being an agent of the Greater Will, Enia supports the Tarnished burning down the Erdtree once her Two Fingers stop communicating with her.
Enia claims that before the Tarnished, another person had gathered two Great Runes.
Radagon is characterized by flowing red hair and is Queen Marika's second chosen consort and a great warrior.
Radagon reportedly hated the red tint of his hair.
A statue in the Royal Capital reveals that Marika and Radagon are one and the same being.
Upon becoming consort, Godfrey took Beast Regent Serosh upon his back to quell his bloodlust and become more fit to be a Lord.
Rennala was a young astrologer who, after a chance encounter with the Full Moon, learned its magic and became one of the most powerful glintstone sorcerers.
Despite being shunned, Morgott still loved the Golden Order.
Morgott's dialogue suggests he attempted to claim the throne of Elden Lord but was warded off by the Erdtree.
The Tarnished first encounters Morgott under the pseudonym Margit, blocking their path to challenge Godrick at Stormveil Castle.
Mohg is a son of Queen Marika and Godfrey, and unlike his twin Morgott, fully embraced his accursed Omen nature.

Mohg believed he was a devoted caretaker enabling Miquella's ascension; because he is not an Empyrean and cannot ascend to godhood himself, he hoped to raise Miquella to full godhood and become his consort to claim the title of monarch.
Miquella, cursed with eternal youth, seeks to achieve godhood by completing a ritual involving capturing Radahn's soul and placing it into Mohg's body.
Miquella's connection to St. Trina, revealed in the DLC, shows they are two manifestations of the same being, echoing the duality of Radagon and Marika.
Messmer, son of Marika and brother to Miquella and Malenia, is cursed with the Abyssal Serpent inside him.
Despite being abandoned by Marika, Messmer continues his mission and becomes a dominant figure in the Realm of Shadow.

Key NPCs met in the Realm of Shadow include Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella; Redmane Freyja, a former Radahn warrior; a Hornsent representative; and Sir Ansbach, a former servant of Mohg.

Early in the DLC it is revealed these characters were united under Miquella's charm, and when he breaks a rune arc to free them, the group becomes divided and uncertain, revealing his manipulative side.
St. Trina, an enigmatic figure barely mentioned in the base game, is explored further through interactions with her and her follower Thiollier, revealing her connection to Miquella.
Sir Ansbach is a former servant of Mohg who now follows Miquella in the Realm of Shadow.
Ansbach was once part of the Pureblood Knights, though the crest on his armor has nearly faded over time.
Despite knowing his loyalty to Mohg is neither logical nor just, Ansbach still holds onto his oath, reflecting an inner struggle.

Redmane Freyja was once deeply loyal to General Radahn, having fought alongside him in past battles, but became a devoted follower of Miquella after he healed a scarlet rot wound on her helmet, leaving a permanent scar she now views as her guiding compass.
Freyja urges the Tarnished to follow the footprints of Miquella, expressing readiness to fight again and a duty to understand and honor the vow Miquella made with Radahn.
Freyja reflects on the complexity of potentially fighting alongside or against former allies like Sir Ansbach.
Hornsent holds a deep grudge against the Erdtree, viewing it as an enemy of his people.
Hornsent views Marika as a betrayer of his people.
Despite his hatred, Hornsent follows an oath to Miquella and offers assistance to the player.
Hornsent provides maps marking crosses tied to his people's suffering as the player aligns with Miquella.
Hornsent refuses to accept alms or gifts out of pride, but rewards the player with maps and guidance if aided.
After Messmer's death, Hornsent expresses satisfaction but states his thirst for vengeance extends to Marika and the entire Erdtree.
Igon is a broken drake warrior consumed by pain and a burning need for revenge against the dread dragon Bayle.
Igon once sought honor through Dragon Communion, shown by the design of his armor pieces.
Igon's soul clings to the mountain where his battle with Bayle took place, and he asks the player to climb the peak to face the dragon.
When the player defeats the Jagged Peak Drake, Igon reflects on the warrior he once was before asking the player to continue his fight against Bayle.
The Dragon Communion Priestess compares Igon's ambition and hunger to Bayle's fiery spirit and relentless drive.
After Bayle is defeated, Igon's spirit is freed and finally able to rest, his revenge realized.
Moore is a gentle giant, a follower of Miquella, and a member of the Forager Brood, a group dedicated to finding crafting materials and recipes across the Land of Shadow.
When the Great Rune breaks, Moore is visibly affected but continues clinging to his devotion to Miquella.
Moore provides Thiollier with Black Syrup after being asked to find it.
If a member of the forager brood is killed or harmed, Moore reacts with grief and anger, calling it an unforgivable tragedy.
After the final boss is defeated, Moore laments the loss of his brood and the absence of allies including Lady Leda, Father Dane, Sir Ansbach, Freyja, Thiollier, and the Hornsent.
Needle Knight Leda is the leader of Miquella's band of followers in the Realm of Shadow.
Leda references Dane, a silent monk who has served Miquella longer than she has, describing him as reserved but a formidable warrior.
After the Great Rune breaks, Leda grows suspicious of her fellow followers and proposes eliminating the Hornsent, fearing his vengeance could threaten Miquella's cause.
Leda identifies Sir Ansbach, a former commander of the Pureblood Knights, as a potential danger due to his past involvement with Miquella's blood blade.
After defeating Sir Ansbach, Leda reflects on the weight of her actions but accepts them as the price for ensuring Miquella's continued favor.
Thiollier is a non-combatant Tarnished character skilled in crafting poison rather than fighting, found at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace.
Thiollier serves Miquella and mentions Lady Leda when first met, acknowledging shared devotion to the same deity.
After the Great Rune breaks, Thiollier becomes haunted by memories of St. Trina, the goddess of slumber, and longs for her poison to grant him eternal sleep.
Thiollier travels to find St. Trina's resting place in the southern part of the world, becoming increasingly obsessive and erratic.
Thiollier eventually becomes hostile, accusing the player of lying if they try to speak for St. Trina, leading to a final confrontation.
Hornsent Grandam belongs to the ancient Hornsent race that once thrived in Belurat Tower Settlement and was connected to the Divine Beast Dancing Lion.
Hornsent Grandam greets the Tarnished with suspicion, accusing them of complicity in Messmer's atrocities.
Dryleaf Dane is a master of unarmed martial combat, a devoted follower of Miquella, and a sworn ally of Leda.
Count Ymir is the High Priest of Manus Metyr Cathedral and a vendor for glintstone sorceries.
Count Ymir shares philosophical musings about the Greater Will, the Erdtree, and the world's flaws.
Count Ymir's companion Jolán can be summoned during specific encounters once her questline advances.
The Dragon Communion Priestess is a surviving Ancient Dragon and worshipper of Dragonlord Placidusax.
Jolán is a loyal warrior serving Count Ymir, found standing on a pillar beside him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr.
Jolán warns the player that crossing Count Ymir will bring regret, though she shows respect if the player earns his trust.
Jolán calls Count Ymir a guiding star in the dark sky and believes him to be the only true light in the night.
If the player betrays or harms Count Ymir, Jolán will fight to protect his will.
Fire Knight Queelign is a knight loyal to Queen Marika, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
Fire Knight Queelign is first encountered as an NPC invader in Belurat Tower Settlement and the Church of Crusade.
